content.user_title: Add Backend HTTP Outcalls to Caffeine AI
content.value_statement: Backend canisters often need to call external APIs without moving requests to the frontend. This skill shows how to use Caffeine AI HTTP outcalls with Motoko GET and POST patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to perform HTTP outcalls from a backend canister.
Introduces the Caffeine AI Motoko outcall module and its request helpers.
Shows the required transform callback pattern for HTTP outcall responses.
Provides a GET request example for backend Motoko code.
Notes that POST usage follows the same module pattern.
limitations: It does not provide JSON parsing utilities for Motoko.
It does not include authentication, rate limiting, or retry guidance.
It does not validate request URLs or response payloads for applications.
It focuses on Caffeine AI backend canisters, not frontend requests.

use_cases.title: Connect a Caffeine AI App to an API
use_cases.description: Add backend HTTP calls when app data must come from an external service.

use_cases.title: Move Network Calls Behind the Backend
use_cases.description: Keep frontend code simpler by routing API requests through the backend canister.

use_cases.title: Prototype External Service Integrations
use_cases.description: Test GET and POST outcall patterns before adding application validation and response handling.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Basic GET Outcall
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a backend API call.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add a backend GET outcall in my Caffeine AI app. Explain the Motoko pieces I need.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt an API Endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me adapt the GET outcall example for this API endpoint: [endpoint]. Include headers I should pass from backend code.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Response Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a backend outcall flow that calls an external service, transforms the response, and returns plain text to the frontend.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Outcall Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my backend outcall design for URL validation, header handling, response transformation, and where JSON parsing should happen.

output_examples.input: User asks for backend GET outcall wiring.
output_examples.output: The assistant describes the module import, transform callback, and request helper sequence without frontend network calls.

output_examples.input: User asks where to parse API JSON.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends returning response text to the frontend and parsing JSON there.
The assistant explains that POST follows the same transform pattern and requires request body handling.

best_practices: Keep HTTP outcalls in backend canister logic when the API must not be called from the frontend.
Validate destination URLs and headers before sending requests from application code.
Plan frontend JSON parsing when Motoko parsing support is not available.
anti_patterns: Do not expose a public backend method that forwards arbitrary URLs without validation.
Do not place secrets or sensitive tokens in prompts or generated examples.
Do not parse complex JSON in Motoko when the frontend can handle it more safely.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build Caffeine AI backend canister calls to external HTTP APIs.

faq.question: Does it make requests from the frontend?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on backend canister outcalls.

faq.question: Which language is shown?
faq.answer: The examples use Motoko for the Caffeine AI backend.

faq.question: Does it include JSON parsing?
faq.answer: No. It notes that JSON is better handled by frontend parsing.

faq.question: Does it support POST requests?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill states that POST usage follows the GET pattern.

faq.question: Should I validate URLs?
faq.answer: Yes. Add application-level URL and header validation before exposing outcall functions.
